No grades, no tuition for the founding class, and Sam Altman on the faculty. Andreessen Horowitz, popularly known by their monicker a16z, has spent nearly two decades in identifying, and investing in some of the most disruptive companies of this generation. The legendary investor is now looking to create “AI-native” talent for some of these promising companies, as it launches the Horowitz Andreessen Academy , a highly selective school that positions itself as a direct alternative to your classic four year college degree. Applications are open for the Founding Class Fellowship, a one-year programme starting Fall 2027. It is tuition-free, and includes travel and everything else to start with. Everything after that — a two-year programme the Academy intends to launch in Fall 2028, pending regulatory approval — will cost roughly what an elite private university does. The Academy has raised $42M in funding, led by a16z, with Marc Andreessen and Erik Torenberg on the board. Angels include Tobi Lütke, Garry Tan, Tony Xu, and Adam D’Angelo. It also has ten founding partners, which includes the likes of Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Nvidia among others. Gagan Biyani, the founder of Udemy & Maven, and the one leading this Horowitz Andreessen Academy said, “The focus of The Academy is on building – which we believe is the most valuable thing humans can do to learn to become a productive, curious and happy adult. Our goal is to help high school graduates thrive by cultivating this instinct. Building is an underlying skill that helps you create lifelong friendships, be indispensable at work, create jobs by providing value to society, and discover your inner joy. That’s why we’re doing this”. The Academy is structured around three things: Pursuits, Courses, and Co-ops. Pursuits are personal projects — startup ideas, rabbit holes, quests — that students choose themselves. Courses are short, high-impact programmes — anywhere from two days to four weeks — taught by actual practitioners. And Co-ops are immersive stints at real companies. The Academy launches with ten founding partners — Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, Nvidia, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit, and Stripe — who will co-create curriculum, provide compute access, and offer hands-on learning opportunities. Founding Class Fellows receive $50,000 in compute credits, a $5,000 travel and research budget, and no tuition bill. There are no grades, no tests, and no homework. The Academy is located in the heart of San Francisco. Applications are officially open for the Founding Class Fellowship, the academy’s inaugural one-year program, which will begin in Fall of 2027. Notably, Founding Class Fellowship will be tuition-free. The Tech Portal is published by Blue Box Media Private Limited . Our investors have no influence over our reporting. sources.title: AstroForge is putting AI in command of its next spacecraft
passages: But resources like that aren’t available to startups, so AstroForge , which is developing technology to mine asteroids, is turning to AI.
The company has developed an autonomous control stack for its spacecraft called “Solo,” a transformer-based model made in-house.

AstroForge, founded in 2022 and backed with $56 million in venture funding, has launched two prototype spacecraft, both of which suffered anomalies that prevented them from achieving most of their mission objectives.
In 2025, its Odin spacecraft was launched into deep space, but the company had difficulty communicating with it.
There are a limited number of antennas on Earth big enough to transmit to spacecraft hundreds of thousands of miles away, and the windows of time in which to do it are small.
“Would that have been recoverable with all the data on the spacecraft?

I don’t know, but I can tell you nothing onboard tried it, and I would love something onboard to try if the spacecraft is unrecoverable at launch,” Matthew Gialich, AstroForge’s co-founder and CEO, said.

It created a stack that includes traditional control algorithms, models trained on test data for specific subsystems like power generation or navigation, and an overall intelligence layer trained on about 2,500 sensors in the spacecraft.
AstroForge plans to fly its first autonomous spacecraft in 2027 on the first rocket launched by Stoke Space.
That mission will be backed by NASA and is expected to gather scientific data about the sun.
The company’s third vehicle, DeepSpace-2, is currently set to launch alongside Intuitive Machines’ third moon mission, expected to head for space by the end of 2026.

extraction.body: Fly to an asteroid, land on it, make no mistakes: If only it were that easy. When NASA sends spacecraft to explore the solar system, they build in redundancy and automation. But much of the work is done by teams of flight controllers communicating with the vehicle from Earth. The OSIRIS-REx mission, which rendezvoused with an asteroid in 2018, had 100 operators on each eight-hour shift. But resources like that aren’t available to startups, so AstroForge , which is developing technology to mine asteroids, is turning to AI. The company has developed an autonomous control stack for its spacecraft called “Solo,” a transformer-based model made in-house. AstroForge plans to fly its first autonomous spacecraft in 2027 on the first rocket launched by Stoke Space. That mission will be backed by NASA and is expected to gather scientific data about the sun. That would be an accomplishment: Most spacecraft autonomy depends on traditional control algorithms due to concerns about the unreliability of neural networks. The first use of a neural network to control a satellite’s positioning in orbit took place just last year . AstroForge, founded in 2022 and backed with $56 million in venture funding, has launched two prototype spacecraft, both of which suffered anomalies that prevented them from achieving most of their mission objectives. In 2025, its Odin spacecraft was launched into deep space, but the company had difficulty communicating with it. There are a limited number of antennas on Earth big enough to transmit to spacecraft hundreds of thousands of miles away, and the windows of time in which to do it are small. Ultimately, AstroForge couldn’t gain control of Odin, but the experience spurred it to consider alternatives: Could it put sufficient intelligence onboard the spacecraft for it to solve its own problems? “Would that have been recoverable with all the data on the spacecraft? I don’t know, but I can tell you nothing onboard tried it, and I would love something onboard to try if the spacecraft is unrecoverable at launch,” Matthew Gialich, AstroForge’s co-founder and CEO, said. “The trade for me is: Do I go build my own ground network, which is going to cost [around] $200 million to put up five dishes around the world and then do operations on it, or do I try to remove it with a model?” Armand Awad, AstroForge’s head of flight software, said the company decided to leverage the advances in transformer models driven by the frontier labs. It created a stack that includes traditional control algorithms, models trained on test data for specific subsystems like power generation or navigation, and an overall intelligence layer trained on about 2,500 sensors in the spacecraft. “I’m not saying I’m going to make general spacecraft autonomy or general autonomy for the world,” Gialich said. “I’m making a constrained autonomy at a very low sensor input, following the basic training of a transformer model.” In theory, the agent in control of the spacecraft will perform tasks like anomaly resolution. Awad imagines it realizing that it has lost track of its position in space, correlating a power anomaly to issues in its star tracker, and fixing the whole thing — “probably turning it on and off in this case.” The company’s third vehicle, DeepSpace-2, is currently set to launch alongside Intuitive Machines’ third moon mission, expected to head for space by the end of 2026. Solo will be onboard that vehicle, flying in “shadow mode,” so AstroForge’s engineers can put it through its paces before the Autonomy-1 mission. Will this truly be an AI agent operating an independent spacecraft? “I don’t plan on flying radios that can receive from Earth on Autonomy-1,” Gialich said. “We have to go all in right now. The move represents one of the first commercial deployments of modern AI architecture in deep space operations, potentially reshaping how we approach autonomous space missions when human oversight isn't practical. AstroForge just announced a game-changing approach to space exploration that could redefine how we operate beyond Earth's orbit. The space mining startup revealed that their upcoming Autonomy-1 mission will be commanded by a small but sophisticated transformer-based AI model, marking what appears to be the first commercial deployment of modern AI architecture in deep space operations. When you're operating millions of miles from Earth, the communication delays make real-time human control impossible. Traditional spacecraft rely on pre-programmed sequences and basic rule-based systems, but AstroForge is betting that transformer models - the same architecture powering ChatGPT and other large language models - can handle the complex decision-making required for asteroid mining operations. This represents a massive technical leap from current space operations. Most spacecraft today operate on relatively simple command sequences uploaded from Earth, with limited ability to adapt to unexpected situations. The transformer model aboard Autonomy-1 will need to process sensor data, make navigation decisions, and potentially identify valuable asteroid targets without waiting for instructions from mission control. The implications extend far beyond AstroForge's immediate mission goals. If successful, this approach could establish a new paradigm for deep space exploration, where AI-powered spacecraft operate as truly autonomous agents rather than remote-controlled robots. NASA and other space agencies have been experimenting with AI in space for years, but mostly in supporting roles rather than primary command functions. Transformer models typically require significant computational resources, but spacecraft operate under strict power and processing constraints. AstroForge will need to demonstrate that their compressed AI model can maintain reliability in the harsh radiation environment of space while making split-second decisions that could determine mission success or failure. For the broader space industry, Autonomy-1 could signal the beginning of a new era where AI becomes the standard approach for deep space missions. Companies like SpaceX and Blue Origin have focused primarily on launch capabilities and near-Earth operations, but autonomous AI could be the key to unlocking more ambitious missions to asteroids, Mars, and beyond. The timing aligns with growing investor interest in space technology and AI applications. AstroForge has positioned itself at the intersection of two of the hottest tech sectors, potentially creating a blueprint that other space startups will rush to follow. The success or failure of Autonomy-1 won't just determine the company's future - it could influence how the entire industry approaches autonomous space operations. What makes this particularly intriguing is the potential for AI spacecraft to learn and adapt during their missions. Unlike traditional systems that operate within fixed parameters, transformer-based models could theoretically improve their performance as they encounter new situations, making each subsequent mission more capable than the last. AstroForge's decision to entrust spacecraft command to AI represents more than just a technological upgrade - it's a fundamental shift toward truly autonomous space exploration. If Autonomy-1 succeeds, we could be looking at the dawn of an era where AI-powered spacecraft operate as independent explorers, making discoveries and decisions millions of miles from human oversight. The success of this mission won't just validate AstroForge's approach; it could establish the template for how humanity explores the solar system in the decades ahead.

extraction.body: Fly to an asteroid, land on it, make no mistakes: If only it were that easy. When NASA sends spacecraft to explore the solar system, they build in redundancy and automation. But much of the work is done by teams of flight controllers communicating with the vehicle from Earth. The OSIRIS-REx mission, which rendezvoused with an asteroid in 2018, had 100 operators on each eight-hour shift. But resources like that aren’t available to startups, so AstroForge , which is developing technology to mine asteroids, is turning to AI. The company has developed an autonomous control stack for its spacecraft called “Solo,” a transformer-based model made in-house. AstroForge plans to fly its first autonomous spacecraft in 2027 on the first rocket launched by Stoke Space. That mission will be backed by NASA and is expected to gather scientific data about the sun. That would be an accomplishment: Most spacecraft autonomy depends on traditional control algorithms due to concerns about the unreliability of neural networks. The first use of a neural network to control a satellite’s positioning in orbit took place just last year . AstroForge, founded in 2022 and backed with $56 million in venture funding, has launched two prototype spacecraft, both of which suffered anomalies that prevented them from achieving most of their mission objectives. In 2025, its Odin spacecraft was launched into deep space, but the company had difficulty communicating with it. There are a limited number of antennas on Earth big enough to transmit to spacecraft hundreds of thousands of miles away, and the windows of time in which to do it are small. Ultimately, AstroForge couldn’t gain control of Odin, but the experience spurred it to consider alternatives: Could it put sufficient intelligence onboard the spacecraft for it to solve its own problems? “Would that have been recoverable with all the data on the spacecraft? I don’t know, but I can tell you nothing onboard tried it, and I would love something onboard to try if the spacecraft is unrecoverable at launch,” Matthew Gialich, AstroForge’s co-founder and CEO, said. “The trade for me is: Do I go build my own ground network, which is going to cost [around] $200 million to put up five dishes around the world and then do operations on it, or do I try to remove it with a model?” Armand Awad, AstroForge’s head of flight software, said the company decided to leverage the advances in transformer models driven by the frontier labs. It created a stack that includes traditional control algorithms, models trained on test data for specific subsystems like power generation or navigation, and an overall intelligence layer trained on about 2,500 sensors in the spacecraft. “I’m not saying I’m going to make general spacecraft autonomy or general autonomy for the world,” Gialich said. “I’m making a constrained autonomy at a very low sensor input, following the basic training of a transformer model.” In theory, the agent in control of the spacecraft will perform tasks like anomaly resolution. Awad imagines it realizing that it has lost track of its position in space, correlating a power anomaly to issues in its star tracker, and fixing the whole thing — “probably turning it on and off in this case.” The company’s third vehicle, DeepSpace-2, is currently set to launch alongside Intuitive Machines’ third moon mission, expected to head for space by the end of 2026. Solo will be onboard that vehicle, flying in “shadow mode,” so AstroForge’s engineers can put it through its paces before the Autonomy-1 mission. Will this truly be an AI agent operating an independent spacecraft? “I don’t plan on flying radios that can receive from Earth on Autonomy-1,” Gialich said. “We have to go all in right now. “Would that have been recoverable with all the data on the spacecraft? I don’t know, but I can tell you nothing onboard tried it, and I would love something onboard to try if the spacecraft is unrecoverable at launch,” Matthew Gialich, AstroForge’s co-founder and CEO, said.

“The trade for me is: Do I go build my own ground network, which is going to cost [around] $200 million to put up five dishes around the world and then do operations on it, or do I try to remove it with a model?”

Armand Awad, AstroForge’s head of flight software, said the company decided to leverage the advances in transformer models driven by the frontier labs. It created a stack that includes traditional control algorithms, models trained on test data for specific subsystems like power generation or navigation, and an overall intelligence layer trained on about 2,500 sensors in the spacecraft.

“I’m not saying I’m going to make general spacecraft autonomy or general autonomy for the world,” Gialich said. “I’m making a constrained autonomy at a very low sensor input, following the basic training of a transformer model.”

In theory, the agent in control of the spacecraft will perform tasks like anomaly resolution. Awad imagines it realizing that it has lost track of its position in space, correlating a power anomaly to issues in its star tracker, and fixing the whole thing — “probably turning it on and off in this case.”

The company’s third vehicle, DeepSpace-2, is currently set to launch alongside Intuitive Machines’ third moon mission, expected to head for space by the end of 2026. Solo will be onboard that vehicle, flying in “shadow mode,” so AstroForge’s engineers can put it through its paces before the Autonomy-1 mission.

Will this truly be an AI agent operating an independent spacecraft? “I don’t plan on flying radios that can receive from Earth on Autonomy-1,” Gialich said. “We have to go all in right now. The team’s probably going to talk me into it by the time we fly it. But right now, I’m telling them no radios.”

passages: Space mining startup AstroForge is making a bold leap into AI-powered space exploration with Autonomy-1, their next spacecraft that will operate under the command of a compact transformer-based AI model.
AstroForge's decision to entrust spacecraft command to AI represents more than just a technological upgrade - it's a fundamental shift toward truly autonomous space exploration.

Traditional spacecraft rely on pre-programmed sequences and basic rule-based systems, but AstroForge is betting that transformer models - the same architecture powering ChatGPT and other large language models - can handle the complex decision-making required for asteroid mining operations.

AstroForge will need to demonstrate that their compressed AI model can maintain reliability in the harsh radiation environment of space while making split-second decisions that could determine mission success or failure.
Most spacecraft today operate on relatively simple command sequences uploaded from Earth, with limited ability to adapt to unexpected situations.
The implications extend far beyond AstroForge's immediate mission goals.
What makes this particularly intriguing is the potential for AI spacecraft to learn and adapt during their missions.
The success of this mission won't just validate AstroForge's approach; it could establish the template for how humanity explores the solar system in the decades ahead.

extraction.body: Space mining startup AstroForge is making a bold leap into AI-powered space exploration with Autonomy-1, their next spacecraft that will operate under the command of a compact transformer-based AI model. The move represents one of the first commercial deployments of modern AI architecture in deep space operations, potentially reshaping how we approach autonomous space missions when human oversight isn't practical. AstroForge just announced a game-changing approach to space exploration that could redefine how we operate beyond Earth's orbit. The space mining startup revealed that their upcoming Autonomy-1 mission will be commanded by a small but sophisticated transformer-based AI model, marking what appears to be the first commercial deployment of modern AI architecture in deep space operations. When you're operating millions of miles from Earth, the communication delays make real-time human control impossible. Traditional spacecraft rely on pre-programmed sequences and basic rule-based systems, but AstroForge is betting that transformer models - the same architecture powering ChatGPT and other large language models - can handle the complex decision-making required for asteroid mining operations. This represents a massive technical leap from current space operations. Most spacecraft today operate on relatively simple command sequences uploaded from Earth, with limited ability to adapt to unexpected situations. The transformer model aboard Autonomy-1 will need to process sensor data, make navigation decisions, and potentially identify valuable asteroid targets without waiting for instructions from mission control. The implications extend far beyond AstroForge's immediate mission goals. If successful, this approach could establish a new paradigm for deep space exploration, where AI-powered spacecraft operate as truly autonomous agents rather than remote-controlled robots. NASA and other space agencies have been experimenting with AI in space for years, but mostly in supporting roles rather than primary command functions. Transformer models typically require significant computational resources, but spacecraft operate under strict power and processing constraints. AstroForge will need to demonstrate that their compressed AI model can maintain reliability in the harsh radiation environment of space while making split-second decisions that could determine mission success or failure. For the broader space industry, Autonomy-1 could signal the beginning of a new era where AI becomes the standard approach for deep space missions. Companies like SpaceX and Blue Origin have focused primarily on launch capabilities and near-Earth operations, but autonomous AI could be the key to unlocking more ambitious missions to asteroids, Mars, and beyond. The timing aligns with growing investor interest in space technology and AI applications. AstroForge has positioned itself at the intersection of two of the hottest tech sectors, potentially creating a blueprint that other space startups will rush to follow. The success or failure of Autonomy-1 won't just determine the company's future - it could influence how the entire industry approaches autonomous space operations. What makes this particularly intriguing is the potential for AI spacecraft to learn and adapt during their missions. Unlike traditional systems that operate within fixed parameters, transformer-based models could theoretically improve their performance as they encounter new situations, making each subsequent mission more capable than the last. AstroForge's decision to entrust spacecraft command to AI represents more than just a technological upgrade - it's a fundamental shift toward truly autonomous space exploration. If Autonomy-1 succeeds, we could be looking at the dawn of an era where AI-powered spacecraft operate as independent explorers, making discoveries and decisions millions of miles from human oversight. The success of this mission won't just validate AstroForge's approach; it could establish the template for how humanity explores the solar system in the decades ahead.

passages: TEMPO.CO, Jakarta - US President Donald Trump has said he is forming an "AI force," as many, including those from within the industry, have recently sounded the alarm about the dangers of Artificial Intelligence continuing to grow unchecked.In a social media post on Saturday, Trump said he will announce an "AI czar" to lead the force soon.The US president continued to brush off warnings about AI's dangers from experts and the AI industry itself as "hoaxes" pushed by the Democrats.What did Trump say about the 'AI force'?While dismissing warnings about AI, Trump still vowed to be "be looking for BAD, and we can do that, very easily, with our already existing criminal and civil justice system.""For this purpose, I am forming the AI Force, much like I did Space Force, which has been a tremendous SUCCESS, in my first term.

"We are leading China, and the rest of the World, and I intend to keep it that way!"Trump compared the criticism of the unchecked, ultrafast growth of AI to what he called other "hoaxes," listing efforts to impeach him, transgender rights and global warming as examples.Why have there been growing calls for regulating AI?Some of the top names in AI said earlier this week they were working on creating a standards body they say would regulate the industry.

extraction.body: Do Trump's task force and a special envoy for artificial intelligence in the US indicate a move toward regulating this disputed technology, particularly vis-a-vis China? Developers warning against their own technologies and a government unwilling to take action — that was the situation in the first half of September amid concerns in the US that AI models were becoming too powerful. Several developers and decision-makers from major AI companies had also called for slowing down the development of the technology . In response, US President Donald Trump posted one of his typical all-caps tweets on his social media platform Truth Social: "AI taking over the World, destroying Humanity, and all other things bad, is a HOAX." Trump also asked "Concerning AI, when, in the History of Business, did anyone see the Leaders of an Industry call for Regulation that, if strongly implemented, will drive them into oblivion and bankruptcy?" Against this backdrop, it comes as something of a surprise that Trump announced over the weekend — following yet another tirade about various alleged Democratic scams — that he would establish an "AI Force" and appoint a special envoy to address the issue. In his post, Trump promised that he would by no means slow down the industry's growth. "However, we will also be looking for BAD, and we can do that, very easily, with our already existing Criminal and Civil Justice System," he wrote. "To that end, I will be announcing, in the near future, the AI 'Czar' — Only High I.Q. individuals need apply!" he added. Trump left open exactly what the individual's duties and powers would be and what resources would be allocated to the position. Trump's announcement could be an attempt to undermine an initiative by California's Democratic Governor Gavin Newsom. The previous day, Newsom had announced plans to establish a commission to regulate Silicon Valley-based tech companies. Among other things, Newsom wants to require these companies to build an emergency shut-off switch into their programs, which would allow humans to stop AI agents that have spun out of control. Several states, including some led by Republicans, are pushing for regulation. The current "AI race" between the US and China is often compared to the space race between the US and the former Soviet Union in the 1960s. Several US companies are currently considered industry leaders. To ensure this remains the case, Trump intends to continue giving them free rein. However, this is not just about economic interests. There is concern that Chinese dominance in artificial intelligence could also lead to Beijing's rise as the sole superpower. In a widely discussed essay , Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, not only warned of the consequences of continued unchecked AI development; he also outlined the potential consequences of the AI competition between the US and China. "If we greatly restrain our AI capabilities in the belief that China will do the same, and then China defects, AI could be so powerful that such a defection could lead to their geopolitical dominance. Therefore any agreement must either have ironclad verifiability, or must be limited enough that defection would not be militarily existential," Amodei wrote. In China, technological developments have traditionally been much more closely tied to governmental objectives. As early as 2017, the State Council of China issued a development plan for a new generation of artificial intelligence. Another strategy paper sets out milestones through which China aims to achieve global dominance in the field of AI by 2030. On Thursday, Trump will host Chinese President Xi Jinping at a state dinner at the White House. The topic of AI is likely to be very high on the agenda.

The US already proposed establishing a mechanism for exchanging information about serious risks posed by AI . The proposal was discussed at a meeting between Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday in New York.

"We think that, just like with any cross-border activity, that moving from opaque to more transparency between the number one and the number two AI powers in the world is very important," Bessent said.

Whether they actually decide to act on this will likely be left up to the two presidents. After all, for them, potential transparency obligations regarding AI are by no means the only point of contention in the negotiations.

22, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- Accenture (NYSE: ACN) and Google Cloud today announced that Volvo Cars has become the lead industry partner for Horizon , an open-source software development platform that helps car makers and automotive suppliers build, test, and deploy software for Android Automotive Operating System (AAOS) more efficiently.
Insights from this collaboration will help refine the platform and expand its generative AI capabilities for automotive companies and other industrial manufacturers.
"Software now defines the automotive brand," said Henry Bzeih, Global Director, Automotive Industry, Google Cloud.
This is how next generation digital experiences reach drivers at agile speed."
"Horizon enables a faster, more flexible and efficient way to deliver software-defined vehicle features.

Its standardized, repeatable and scalable processes help deliver reliable, high-quality software products, while significantly reducing time to market," said Juergen Reers, Global Automotive & Mobility Lead, Accenture.
"Horizon will allow Volvo Cars' engineers to focus on what matters most: creating differentiated vehicle experiences and continuously delivering new value to drivers through software at high speed."

The platform will give its engineers access to faster development workflows, virtual testing environments and AI-assisted software development tools, freeing engineering teams to spend more time building in-car experiences.
"We're building some of the most complex products in the world, which requires a development environment built to match," said Gregor Zetsche, Head of Connected Experience at Volvo Cars.

MIAMI, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Nucleus Research has published its inaugural 2026 Workforce Planning and Analytics Technology Value Matrix, examining a market where organizations are connecting workforce costs, capacity, and skills more closely with business planning. Finance, HR, and operations teams are prioritizing forecast accuracy, planning efficiency, scenario modeling, and stronger alignment between staffing requirements and business demand. Customer ROI is supported by reducing spreadsheet maintenance, shortening planning cycles, and improving the accuracy of headcount and compensation forecasts. Vendors are investing in common workforce data models, prebuilt connectors, and deeper integrations with HR, payroll, recruiting, finance, and enterprise data platforms. These capabilities create a more consistent planning foundation and help organizations incorporate workforce changes while maintaining control over assumptions and approved plans. "Workforce planning delivers greater value when organizations can evaluate the financial and operational impact of workforce decisions within the same planning process," said Charlotte Belke , Research Analyst at Nucleus Research . "Connecting cost, capacity, and workforce requirements gives teams the information needed to make more accurate plans and respond faster as business conditions change." AI is extending planning capabilities through natural language tools that investigate variances, generate forecasts, build models, and apply scenario assumptions. Role-based agents are also expanding access to workforce and financial information, with value determined by the planning effort removed and the ability of users to validate and approve outputs. Scenario modeling is another area of continued investment. Organizations can compare hiring, development, redeployment, and staffing alternatives against cost and capacity requirements before execution. Deeper connections with recruiting and workforce management systems are also helping translate approved workforce plans into operational action, supporting faster planning cycles and stronger returns from technology investments. Leaders in the Value Matrix excel in both functionality and usability, offering comprehensive solutions that deliver high ROI and support large-scale adoption. Leaders in this year's Value Matrix include Anaplan, Crunchr, Gloat, Logile, UKG, Visier, and Zebra Technologies. Expert vendors offer deep, specialized functionality suited for complex requirements. These include OneStream, Oracle, Orgvue, Prophix, SAP, and Workday. Accelerators focus on usability and ease of deployment, providing simpler solutions that enable quick adoption with less complexity. This year's Accelerators are ChartHop, Dayforce, Eightfold, Infor, Pigment, Planful, and Vena. Core Providers offer essential, reliable functionalities, ideal for organizations with basic needs. This year's Core Providers are Board, Jedox, LYTIQS, One Model, ProHance, Talentia, and TeamOhana. Nucleus Research is the recognized global leader in ROI technology research. Using a case-based approach, we provide research streams and advisory services that allow vendors and end users to quantify and maximize the return from their technology investments. For more information, visit NucleusResearch.com or follow our latest updates on LinkedIn.

MIAMI, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Nucleus Research has published its inaugural 2026 Workforce Planning and Analytics Technology Value Matrix, examining a market where organizations are connecting workforce costs, capacity, and skills more closely with business planning. Finance, HR, and operations teams are prioritizing forecast accuracy, planning efficiency, scenario modeling, and stronger alignment between staffing requirements and business demand. Customer ROI is supported by reducing spreadsheet maintenance, shortening planning cycles, and improving the accuracy of headcount and compensation forecasts. Vendors are investing in common workforce data models, prebuilt connectors, and deeper integrations with HR, payroll, recruiting, finance, and enterprise data platforms. These capabilities create a more consistent planning foundation and help organizations incorporate workforce changes while maintaining control over assumptions and approved plans. "Workforce planning delivers greater value when organizations can evaluate the financial and operational impact of workforce decisions within the same planning process," said Charlotte Belke , Research Analyst at Nucleus Research . "Connecting cost, capacity, and workforce requirements gives teams the information needed to make more accurate plans and respond faster as business conditions change." AI is extending planning capabilities through natural language tools that investigate variances, generate forecasts, build models, and apply scenario assumptions. Role-based agents are also expanding access to workforce and financial information, with value determined by the planning effort removed and the ability of users to validate and approve outputs. Scenario modeling is another area of continued investment. Organizations can compare hiring, development, redeployment, and staffing alternatives against cost and capacity requirements before execution. Deeper connections with recruiting and workforce management systems are also helping translate approved workforce plans into operational action, supporting faster planning cycles and stronger returns from technology investments. Leaders in the Value Matrix excel in both functionality and usability, offering comprehensive solutions that deliver high ROI and support large-scale adoption. Leaders in this year's Value Matrix include Anaplan, Crunchr, Gloat, Logile, UKG, Visier, and Zebra Technologies. Expert vendors offer deep, specialized functionality suited for complex requirements. These include OneStream, Oracle, Orgvue, Prophix, SAP, and Workday. Accelerators focus on usability and ease of deployment, providing simpler solutions that enable quick adoption with less complexity. This year's Accelerators are ChartHop, Dayforce, Eightfold, Infor, Pigment, Planful, and Vena. Core Providers offer essential, reliable functionalities, ideal for organizations with basic needs. This year's Core Providers are Board, Jedox, LYTIQS, One Model, ProHance, Talentia, and TeamOhana. Nucleus Research is the recognized global leader in ROI technology research. Using a case-based approach, we provide research streams and advisory services that allow vendors and end users to quantify and maximize the return from their technology investments. For more information, visit NucleusResearch.com or follow our latest updates on LinkedIn.

extraction.body: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 is built around one question for founders: How do you build an enduring company in the AI era? For investors, it's the opposite: How do you find that company before someone else does? At Disrupt, the volume and competition are the point for investors, not a drawback. Year after year, investors who've explored the Expo Halls, met founders, and learned from peers at panels and Side Events have proven why you need to be on the ground to get ahead of the curve. Consider that every founder pitching during the Startup Battlefield competition does so in front of a packed room of VCs. Why? Because they know their next cohort could be sitting right there. All it takes is making the trip to San Francisco this October 13-15 . This guide is for the investors who recognize that three days spent at Moscone West are well worth it and who plan to walk away with the insights and prospects that yield returns. Disrupt features numerous tracks, depending on the check sizes you're able to write and the stage of startup you specialize in. If you're coming to build out your portfolio of early bets and get in on rounds before they're priced, prioritize the Startup Battlefield 200 semifinalist pitches, the Builders Stage , and the Expo Hall . Disrupt will be all about volume and speed of qualified deal flow. Prioritize the founder list, our curated 1:1 meetings, and the Deal Flow Café. This stage is best suited for those coming to the event as much for market intelligence and strategic partnership scouting as for deal sourcing. Prioritize the Smart Money and Smart Systems Stages, as well as the exclusive StrictlyVC investor-only session. More than 20,000 curated meetings take place over just three days, within dedicated environments like investor receptions and structured networking sessions. Investor-founder connections aren't hallway luck –they're built into Disrupt's infrastructure. You get direct access to 200 pitch-ready, TechCrunch-vetted startups through Startup Battlefield 200 . And we'll put an emphasis on "vetted." Our Startup Battlefield team, working alongside TechCrunch's incredibly discerning team of editors and writers, has done a significant amount of diligence for you already. Past speakers have included investors like Elad Gil and Vinod Khosla, and this year's lineup puts you in the room with the operators you're underwriting, too. We're talking Rivian's RJ Scaringe, Amazon's Panos Panay, Replit's Amjad Masad, and Cerebras' Andrew Feldman, just for starters. The Disrupt crowd is your signal. With a mix of 10,000 founders, investors, and operators filling Moscone West, the companies worth knowing will get discovered by someone. This is your chance to make sure it's you. For founders, Startup Battlefield is a visibility engine and a trial by fire. For investors, it's a filtered shortlist that the TechCrunch team has spent months narrowing down for you. Startup Battlefield is intensely competitive. Thousands of global startups apply, while just 200 make the cut and only a handful reach the finals. That funnel is doing your top-of-pipeline filtering for you before you ever take a meeting. If you're not circling around these startups, your competitors are. We have several different passes for Disrupt, and by joining the community via an Investor Pass, you get access to perks like… This is a space exclusively for founders and investors, fostering impromptu run-ins with founders actively seeking capital. Grab coffee or a beverage of choice, explore opportunities, and start conversations that can turn into your next deal. You'll get early access to the full list of Disrupt founders looking for connections with investors. The next addition to your portfolio can be identified before the event even begins, giving you more time to find even more opportunities. Through the Disrupt app, you can schedule 1:1 and small-group meetings with founders matching your focus areas, with AI helping match you by mutual interests instead of waiting on fate. The investors who make the most out of Disrupt don't leave sourcing to chance — they've already scanned the available resources and set up their agendas in advance. Our editorially curated programming, including all three days of sessions and panels, is available here , stretching across six stages, breakout sessions, roundtables, and Side Events. Here are some of the stages that might be of interest: The Smart Money Stage : Interested in capital markets, embedded finance, and stablecoins? Everything within the fintech realm, especially within the intersection of AI, is included. The Smart Systems Stage : It's all about compute, infrastructure, and energy economics. If you need to build a justification for underwriting AI infrastructure bets, this is the place to start. The AI Stage and Real World AI Stages : Get market intelligence on where the fastest-growing startups are deploying, not just building. The Disrupt Stage : This is where operators and CEOs set the narrative your current and future portfolio companies will be measured against. We've gone in depth about the benefits to you, your portfolio, and the opportunities Disrupt offers you. But there are always matters of hotels, expenses, and travel to sort out. Our Disrupt site has the bulk of these issues covered, but to tackle some common questions and pressing opportunities: For your hotel needs , we have partnerships with several stellar hotels near Moscone West. You'll get exclusive discounts, easy access to Disrupt and anything else you might want to explore in San Francisco, and yes, you'll get points for your accommodations. If you're bringing a large cohort or are interested in having a company in your portfolio take part in our Expo Hall to get wider visibility, check out our bulk ticket options here and our Exhibit Table options here . For all other questions, you can explore our full Disrupt page to find more specific FAQs, and we hope to see you in San Francisco this year!

extraction.body: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 is built around one question for founders: How do you build an enduring company in the AI era? For investors, it's the opposite: How do you find that company before someone else does? At Disrupt, the volume and competition are the point for investors, not a drawback. Year after year, investors who've explored the Expo Halls, met founders, and learned from peers at panels and Side Events have proven why you need to be on the ground to get ahead of the curve. Consider that every founder pitching during the Startup Battlefield competition does so in front of a packed room of VCs. Why? Because they know their next cohort could be sitting right there. All it takes is making the trip to San Francisco this October 13-15 . This guide is for the investors who recognize that three days spent at Moscone West are well worth it and who plan to walk away with the insights and prospects that yield returns. Disrupt features numerous tracks, depending on the check sizes you're able to write and the stage of startup you specialize in. If you're coming to build out your portfolio of early bets and get in on rounds before they're priced, prioritize the Startup Battlefield 200 semifinalist pitches, the Builders Stage , and the Expo Hall . Disrupt will be all about volume and speed of qualified deal flow. Prioritize the founder list, our curated 1:1 meetings, and the Deal Flow Café. This stage is best suited for those coming to the event as much for market intelligence and strategic partnership scouting as for deal sourcing. Prioritize the Smart Money and Smart Systems Stages, as well as the exclusive StrictlyVC investor-only session. More than 20,000 curated meetings take place over just three days, within dedicated environments like investor receptions and structured networking sessions. Investor-founder connections aren't hallway luck –they're built into Disrupt's infrastructure. You get direct access to 200 pitch-ready, TechCrunch-vetted startups through Startup Battlefield 200 . And we'll put an emphasis on "vetted." Our Startup Battlefield team, working alongside TechCrunch's incredibly discerning team of editors and writers, has done a significant amount of diligence for you already. Past speakers have included investors like Elad Gil and Vinod Khosla, and this year's lineup puts you in the room with the operators you're underwriting, too. We're talking Rivian's RJ Scaringe, Amazon's Panos Panay, Replit's Amjad Masad, and Cerebras' Andrew Feldman, just for starters. The Disrupt crowd is your signal. With a mix of 10,000 founders, investors, and operators filling Moscone West, the companies worth knowing will get discovered by someone. This is your chance to make sure it's you. For founders, Startup Battlefield is a visibility engine and a trial by fire. For investors, it's a filtered shortlist that the TechCrunch team has spent months narrowing down for you. Startup Battlefield is intensely competitive. Thousands of global startups apply, while just 200 make the cut and only a handful reach the finals. That funnel is doing your top-of-pipeline filtering for you before you ever take a meeting. If you're not circling around these startups, your competitors are. We have several different passes for Disrupt, and by joining the community via an Investor Pass, you get access to perks like… This is a space exclusively for founders and investors, fostering impromptu run-ins with founders actively seeking capital. Grab coffee or a beverage of choice, explore opportunities, and start conversations that can turn into your next deal. You'll get early access to the full list of Disrupt founders looking for connections with investors. The next addition to your portfolio can be identified before the event even begins, giving you more time to find even more opportunities. Through the Disrupt app, you can schedule 1:1 and small-group meetings with founders matching your focus areas, with AI helping match you by mutual interests instead of waiting on fate. The investors who make the most out of Disrupt don't leave sourcing to chance — they've already scanned the available resources and set up their agendas in advance. Our editorially curated programming, including all three days of sessions and panels, is available here , stretching across six stages, breakout sessions, roundtables, and Side Events. Here are some of the stages that might be of interest: The Smart Money Stage : Interested in capital markets, embedded finance, and stablecoins? Everything within the fintech realm, especially within the intersection of AI, is included. The Smart Systems Stage : It's all about compute, infrastructure, and energy economics. If you need to build a justification for underwriting AI infrastructure bets, this is the place to start. The AI Stage and Real World AI Stages : Get market intelligence on where the fastest-growing startups are deploying, not just building. The Disrupt Stage : This is where operators and CEOs set the narrative your current and future portfolio companies will be measured against. We've gone in depth about the benefits to you, your portfolio, and the opportunities Disrupt offers you. But there are always matters of hotels, expenses, and travel to sort out. Our Disrupt site has the bulk of these issues covered, but to tackle some common questions and pressing opportunities: For your hotel needs , we have partnerships with several stellar hotels near Moscone West. You'll get exclusive discounts, easy access to Disrupt and anything else you might want to explore in San Francisco, and yes, you'll get points for your accommodations. If you're bringing a large cohort or are interested in having a company in your portfolio take part in our Expo Hall to get wider visibility, check out our bulk ticket options here and our Exhibit Table options here . For all other questions, you can explore our full Disrupt page to find more specific FAQs, and we hope to see you in San Francisco this year!

The Wall Street Bitcoin ETF takeover has crossed a defining threshold. What began as cautious experimentation has turned into coordinated institutional dominance, with Morgan Stanley joining BlackRock and Fidelity in a Bitcoin ETF market now worth over $123 billion. This reflects the alignment of regulation, client demand, and competitive pressure pulling Bitcoin ( CRYPTO: BTC ) squarely into traditional finance. Cryptocurrency exposure is becoming standard as large banks and asset managers integrate ETFs into advisory products and retirement plans. The outcome is a Bitcoin ETF market that’s shaped by institutional flows and long-term allocations rather than speculative momentum. The Bitcoin ETF story represents one of the fastest institutional adoption cycles in financial history. Decades of SEC denial ended in January 2024 when court decisions compelled the agency to greenlight eleven spot Bitcoin ETFs, eliminating longstanding custody and regulatory concerns. Institutional capital responded immediately. Bitcoin ETFs attracted $35.2 billion in cumulative net inflows in 2024, and the total net assets now stand at $123.52 billion. The first week of 2026 alone brought over $1.2 billion in fresh capital . This regulatory clarity and the availability of regulated structures enabled pension funds, endowments, and wealth managers to invest with confidence, transforming Bitcoin from a speculative asset into an acknowledged commodity exposure. The Wall Street Bitcoin ETF takeover marks a structural shift. Investor confidence grew from regulatory approval and operational readiness, proving that traditional finance could interact with crypto assets safely. Both spot and futures ETFs now form the foundation of institutional crypto involvement. The Morgan Stanley crypto ETF entry on January 6 represents the most significant bank-led Wall Street’s expansion yet. Morgan Stanley filed S-1 registration statements with the SEC for spot Bitcoin and Solana ETFs , becoming the first major U.S. bank to seek approval for its own spot Bitcoin ETF. By integrating a proprietary Bitcoin ETF into E*Trade and wealth management platforms, Morgan Stanley retains control over client relationships, fee structures, and portfolio recommendations. CME Group Inc., the operator of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange and related U.S. futures markets, plans to add Bitcoin Cash and Uniswap futures to its regulated cryptocurrency list later in October. The contracts would let traders hedge or take price exposure without holding the tokens. The listing still depends on regulatory review.

In a September 22, 2026 statement , CME Group said the products are scheduled to start on October 19. The same date appears in the exchange’s cryptocurrency futures frequently asked questions (FAQ). Both notices say the launch remains pending regulatory review.

A futures contract is a standardized agreement that tracks an asset’s price to a set expiry date. CME Group said the Bitcoin Cash and Uniswap contracts would be cash settled. Cash settlement means profits and losses are paid in dollars against a reference price. Traders would not receive Bitcoin Cash (BCH) or Uniswap (UNI) coins at expiry. Settlement would use CME CF reference rates, the same benchmark family already used for the firm’s other cryptocurrency futures.

The planned sizes are 250 BCH for the standard Bitcoin Cash future and 25 BCH for the Micro Bitcoin Cash future. The Uniswap future would cover 10,000 UNI, with a Micro Uniswap future covering 1,000 UNI. CME Group’s Basis Trade at Index Close (BTIC) page also lists both products for October 19, pending review. BTIC lets two parties agree to a futures trade as a spread to a published reference rate.

Bitcoin Cash is a 2017 fork of Bitcoin that kept a larger block size and a payments-focused design. Uniswap is a decentralized exchange (DEX), a venue where users trade tokens through automated liquidity pools rather than a central order book . UNI is the governance token of that protocol . The listing would put a decentralized finance (DeFi) token on the same regulated futures roster as coins such as Solana ( SOL ) and XRP .

CME Group already lists single-asset futures on Bitcoin, Ether, XRP, Solana, Cardano (ADA), Chainlink (LINK), Stellar Lumens (XLM), Avalanche ( AVAX ) and Sui (SUI) , according to the same announcement. Bitcoin Cash is not new to that complex. It was included in the Nasdaq CME Crypto Index when those index futures began trading in June. Uniswap would be a new single-asset listing.

The exchange has spent 2026 widening that menu. It listed Cardano, Chainlink and Stellar futures in February, then prepared Avalanche and Sui futures ahead of near-continuous hours. Cryptocurrency futures and options on the venue moved to a 24 hours a day, 7 days a week (24/7) schedule on May 29. The first weekend of that schedule saw about $50 million in notional trading.

CME Group said first-half 2026 cryptocurrency futures and options averaged 279,800 contracts a day, or $8.3 billion in notional value. Average open interest (OI) , the number of contracts still outstanding, was 264,600 contracts, or $15.4 billion. The 2026 expansion into Cardano, Chainlink, Stellar, Avalanche and Sui futures has contributed more than $1 billion in notional value year to date. Bitcoin and Ether still account for most of that activity.

CME Group Inc. (NASDAQ: CME) last closed at $275.53 on September 21, down $0.48, or 0.17%, according to Yahoo Finance . The previous close was $276.01. The 52-week range is $218.31 to $329.16. Market capitalization was about $99.1 billion. The trailing price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio was 23.37.

The indicated dividend yield was 1.89%. The next earnings date on the quote page is October 21, 2026. Interest rates, equity indexes, and commodity contracts remain the core of the business. Cryptocurrency futures are a growth line, not the franchise.

Giovanni Vicioso, Global Head of Cryptocurrency Products at CME Group, said clients want broader regulated tools as crypto markets mature. Justin Young, chief executive officer (CEO) of Volatility Shares, and Noel Kimmel, president at Ripple Prime, were also quoted in the release. Those comments describe demand from firms that already clear Bitcoin and Ether on CME Group and want the same margin and settlement stack for two more tokens.

Bitcoin Cash has a second market-structure track. Grayscale Investments Sponsors, LLC filed an amended Form S-3 on September 11, 2026, seeking to convert Grayscale Bitcoin Cash Trust (BCH) into a fund listed on NYSE Arca. Form S-3 is a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) registration form. The amendment is not an approval to list or trade. The Crypto Times earlier covered Grayscale’s Bitcoin Cash exchange-traded fund (ETF) paperwork.

Uniswap’s token has had a separate catalyst . UNI rose after the SEC opened a limited path for tokenized U.S. stocks to trade through permissioned automated market maker (AMM) pools, a move the Crypto Times reported on September 18. An AMM pool prices trades with a formula and deposited liquidity rather than a traditional bid-ask book. A futures listing would give funds a regulated hedge against UNI. It would not change how the Uniswap protocol works.

The first users are likely to be market makers, prime brokers, and funds that want price exposure without spot custody . A holder of BCH or UNI can sell the future to hedge inventory. Retail traders who use high-leverage offshore perpetual swaps, contracts with no expiry date, are less likely to move. CME Group is separately contesting the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) over Bitcoin perpetual futures.

A listing is not the same as a liquid market. Solana and XRP futures later drew meaningful open interest. Cardano, Chainlink and Stellar were quieter. Bitcoin Cash had a stronger 2025 large-cap run and has since cooled.

If the October 19 launch clears review, the first useful test will be opening-week volume , open interest, and whether the futures price stays close to the spot market . Until then, the announcement is a product-calendar item, not evidence of demand.

"As crypto markets continue to mature, participants require broader, regulated tools to navigate evolving digital asset related price risk," Giovanni Vicioso, CME Group's global head of cryptocurrency products, said in a statement.
The launch comes as institutional investors seek more ways to hedge exposure to cryptocurrencies beyond Bitcoin (CRYPTO: $BTC) and Ether (CRYPTO: $ETH), according to CME.

The new contracts will add to CME's existing futures offerings covering assets including Bitcoin, Ether, XRP (CRYPTO: $XRP), Solana (CRYPTO: $SOL), Cardano (CRYPTO: $ADA), Chainlink (CRYPTO: $LINK), Stellar (CRYPTO: $XLM), Avalanche (CRYPTO: $AVAX) and Sui (CRYPTO: $SUI).
The planned sizes are 250 BCH for the standard Bitcoin Cash future and 25 BCH for the Micro Bitcoin Cash future.
The Uniswap future would cover 10,000 UNI, with a Micro Uniswap future covering 1,000 UNI.

BTIC lets two parties agree to a futures trade as a spread to a published reference rate.

The listing still depends on regulatory review.

Solana and XRP futures later drew meaningful open interest.

The halving reduces the rate of new Bitcoin creation by half, and that typically jump-starts a blistering Bitcoin rally.

That's why Bitcoin's recent performance is so encouraging for crypto investors: It means Bitcoin may have already bottomed. Bitcoin hit a peak of $126,000 back in October. So it's been nearly a year from peak to trough.
If you buy into the four-year cycle, Bitcoin is due for a recovery. Crypto investors have now survived the one bad year they know they will get from Bitcoin in each cycle.

Moreover, in its entire existence, Bitcoin has never had back-to-back losing years. That makes me think that Bitcoin's recent stinker of a performance in 2025 won't be repeated this year. Right now, Bitcoin is only down less than 2% for the year. A positive year is within sight.

With just a modicum of momentum, Bitcoin could be back in positive territory by the end of October. This, incidentally, happens to be one of the best months of the year for Bitcoin. For good reason, crypto investors refer to October as " Uptober ."

Bitcoin's next halving will take place in April 2028. That leads me to think that the 18 months between then and now will be remarkably bullish for Bitcoin. There is typically an intensifying recovery heading into the halving, followed by an explosion of price activity after the halving.

And I'm not the only one who thinks this. Coinbase Global Chief Executive Officer Brian Armstrong has also suggested that Bitcoin now will rally hard into its April 2028 halving. He's now predicting that Bitcoin could soar as high as $400,000 by 2030.
However, just keep in mind: Past performance is no guarantee of future results. Just because Bitcoin has traded in four-year cycles throughout its existence is no guarantee it will continue to do so.

That's especially the case, given that Bitcoin has no clear catalysts on the horizon. The Clarity Act failed to pass the Senate in mid-September, yet the price of Bitcoin rose. The Federal Reserve hiked interest rates in September, and yet the price of Bitcoin went up. Both factors should have been very negative for Bitcoin. They were not.
So it's up to you to decide whether this Bitcoin rally is for real. Admittedly, it takes some suspension of disbelief to think that Bitcoin can continue to gain ground without a clear catalyst ahead.

Nevertheless, I'm leaning into Bitcoin's historical track record. If history is any guide, Bitcoin has already bottomed, and crypto investors are about to be rewarded for their patience ahead of the 2028 halving.
